assignedReviews.card_evidence: A control plant is kept free of pests
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a control plant in a pest experiment, which is unrelated to the structure of the solar system or celestial objects.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A control plant is kept free of pests
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: distinguish among comets, meteoroids, asteroids, and dwarf planets, and describe how they help us to understand the nature and formation of the Earth and the Solar System
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about a control plant in an experiment, not about comets, meteoroids, asteroids, or dwarf planets.

copy.en: A control plant is kept free of pests so you can compare it with plants that have insects, showing what normal growth looks like.
copy.tl: Ang control plant ay hindi nilalagyan ng pests para maikumpara mo ito sa mga halamang may insekto, at makita kung ano ang normal na pagtubo.
copy.bis: Ang control plant wala butangi og pests aron imo kining maikumpara sa mga tanom nga adunay mga insekto, ug makita nimo ang normal nga pagtubo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In a controlled experiment, you change only the manipulated variable
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the concept of a controlled experiment and manipulated variables, which is unrelated to describing the structure of the solar system, celestial objects, or their composition. The assigned competency G5-E-11 is about the solar system, so the tag is incorrect.

copy.en: In a controlled experiment, you change only the manipulated variable while keeping all other variables the same, so you know what caused the result.
copy.tl: Sa isang controlled experiment, ang manipulated variable lang ang binabago mo habang pinananatiling pareho ang ibang variables, para malaman mo kung ano ang sanhi ng resulta.
copy.bis: Sa usa ka controlled experiment, ang manipulated variable lang ang imong usbon samtang gipabilin nga pareho ang uban nga variables, aron mahibaloan nimo kon unsay hinungdan sa resulta.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An experiment is a controlled scientific study of specific variables
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate various techniques in separating mixtures, such as decantation, winnowing, scooping, picking, evaporation, filtering, sieving, and using magnets
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines a controlled experiment and variables. It contains no content about separating mixtures (decantation, winnowing, filtering, etc.) or any mixture separation technique, so it does not support this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An experiment is a controlled scientific study of specific variables
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the benefits of each mixture separation technique in preparing useful products
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses controlled experiments and variables, not the benefits of mixture separation techniques in preparing useful products. It is unrelated to this competency.

copy.en: An experiment is a controlled scientific study of specific variables, which are factors that can take different values.
copy.tl: Ang experiment ay isang controlled na scientific study ng mga tiyak na variable, na mga factor na pwedeng magkaroon ng iba't ibang halaga.
copy.bis: Ang experiment usa ka controlled nga scientific study sa mga piho nga variable, nga mga factor nga mahimong adunay lain-laing bili.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A controlled variable is what you keep the same in an experiment so the test is fair

assignedReviews.reason: The card defines a controlled variable in experimental design. It does not address changes of state, particle arrangement, or energy changes (solid→liquid→vapor, vapor→liquid→solid).

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A controlled variable is what you keep the same in an experiment so the test is fair
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of heat energy in change of state processes
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about fair-test experimental design, not about the role of heat energy in change of state processes. No connection to melting, evaporation, freezing, or condensation.

copy.en: A controlled variable is what you keep the same in an experiment so the test is fair, like using the same kind of plant when comparing how much water affects growth.
copy.tl: Ang controlled variable ay ang pinananatili mong pareho sa isang experiment para maging patas ang test, tulad ng paggamit ng parehong uri ng halaman kapag kinukumpara kung paano nakakaapekto ang dami ng tubig sa paglaki.
copy.bis: Ang controlled variable mao ang imong gipabilin nga pareho sa usa ka experiment aron patas ang test, sama sa paggamit sa parehong klase sa tanom kon ikumpara kon unsa ang epekto sa gidaghanon sa tubig sa pagtubo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: You can see convection when water boils in a pot, when a hot air balloon rises, or when warm air rises from a burning candle.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different ways that plants reproduce, such as pollination, seed production, and plant propagation
assignedReviews.reason: Everyday convection examples are heat transfer, not plant reproduction.

copy.en: You can see convection when water boils in a pot, when a hot air balloon rises, or when warm air rises from a burning candle.
copy.tl: Makikita mo ang convection kapag kumukulo ang tubig sa kaldero, kapag umaangat ang isang hot air balloon, o kapag umaangat ang mainit na hangin mula sa isang nagniningas na kandila.
copy.bis: Makita nimo ang convection kung magbukal ang tubig sa kaldero, kung mosaka ang usa ka hot air balloon, o kung mosaka ang init nga hangin gikan sa nagdilaab nga kandila.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Convection transfers heat in fluids — liquids and gases — through the bulk movement of the fluid caused by differences in temperature
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches convection in fluids, a physics/earth-science concept, and provides no information about the muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, or respiratory systems. It is unrelated to the competency.

copy.en: Convection is the transfer of heat through the movement of particles in a fluid, like water or air.
copy.tl: Ang convection ay ang paglipat ng heat sa pamamagitan ng paggalaw ng mga particles sa isang fluid, tulad ng tubig o hangin.
copy.bis: Ang convection mao ang pagbalhin sa heat pinaagi sa paglihok sa mga particles sa usa ka fluid, sama sa tubig o hangin.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Inside a nursery, warm air rises and cooler air sinks, creating convection currents that help move heat around the plants.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the parts and functions, and demonstrate proper handling and storing of a compound microscope
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes convection currents in a nursery, a physics/heat-transfer concept. G7-L-1 requires identifying parts and functions of a compound microscope and demonstrating proper handling and storing. There is no microscope content or any living-things equipment content; the card is unrelated to the competency.

copy.en: Inside a nursery, warm air rises and cooler air sinks, creating convection currents that help move heat around the plants.
copy.tl: Sa loob ng nursery, ang mainit na hangin ay tumataas at ang malamig na hangin ay bumababa, kaya nagkakaroon ng convection currents na tumutulong magpalipat-lipat ng init sa paligid ng mga halaman.
copy.bis: Sa sulod sa nursery, ang init nga hangin mosaka ug ang bugnaw nga hangin mokanaog, nga maghimo ug convection currents nga makatabang sa paglihok sa init libot sa mga tanom.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Convergent boundaries create different landforms
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe typical weather conditions before, during, and after a tropical cyclone
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes landforms formed at convergent plate boundaries (trenches, volcanic arcs, mountain ranges). This is a geology/plate-tectonics topic and provides no information about weather conditions before, during, or after a tropical cyclone, which is the subject of G5-E-10.

copy.en: Convergent boundaries create different landforms depending on the plates: trenches and volcanic arcs for oceanic collisions, and mountain ranges for continental collisions.
copy.tl: Ang convergent boundaries ay lumilikha ng iba't ibang anyong lupa depende sa mga plate: trenches at volcanic arcs para sa oceanic collisions, at bulubundukin para sa continental collisions.
copy.bis: Ang convergent boundaries maghimo ug lain-laing mga porma sa yuta depende sa mga plate: trenches ug volcanic arcs para sa oceanic collisions, ug kabukiran para sa continental collisions.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: You multiply the number of moles by the molar mass
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some useful things that people have made from non-living materials and describe what natural materials have been used to make the items
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches mole-to-mass conversion, a chemistry concept. G3-E-2 is about identifying useful things made from non-living materials and their natural sources. No overlap in content or skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: You multiply the number of moles by the molar mass
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that the non-living materials that make up the environment are referred to as 'earth materials'
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about molar mass conversion, not about recognizing non-living materials as 'earth materials'. Completely unrelated to the competency.

copy.en: How do you convert moles to mass?\n\nYou multiply the number of moles by the molar mass, which gives you the mass in grams.
copy.tl:
Paano mo iko-convert ang moles papuntang mass?

Imumultiplika mo ang bilang ng moles sa molar mass, na nagbibigay sa iyo ng mass sa grams.
copy.bis:
Unsaon nimo pag-convert ang moles ngadto sa mass?

Imultiply nimo ang gidaghanon sa moles sa molar mass, nga naghatag nimo sa mass sa grams.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A double convex lens forms images
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about convex lens image formation, an optics topic. G3-L-5 concerns observing outer parts of plants and their roles in water/nutrient uptake. No plant anatomy or function is taught.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A double convex lens forms images
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how plant organs (leaf, stem, roots) work together as the transport system
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes how a convex lens forms images based on object distance. G8-L-3 requires describing how plant organs (leaf, stem, roots) work together as a transport system. The card has no plant transport content.

copy.en: A double convex lens forms images whose location, size, and orientation depend on how far the object is from the lens.
copy.tl: Ang double convex lens ay bumubuo ng images na ang lokasyon, laki, at orientation ay depende sa layo ng object mula sa lens.
copy.bis: Ang double convex lens moporma og mga image nga ang lokasyon, gidak-on, ug oryentasyon nagdepende sa gilay-on sa object gikan sa lens.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A convex lens is thicker at the center than at the edges, and it makes parallel light rays come together at a focal point.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe kinetic energy as the movement of objects or particles, and potential energy as energy stored due to the position of objects or particles
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the shape and focusing behavior of a convex lens, which is a light/optics concept. G8-F-4 requires describing kinetic energy as movement and potential energy as stored energy due to position. The card provides no information about kinetic or potential energy, so it does not support this competency.

copy.en: A convex lens is thicker at the center than at the edges, and it makes parallel light rays come together at a focal point.
copy.tl: Ang convex lens ay mas makapal sa gitna kaysa sa mga gilid, at pinagsasama-sama nito ang parallel light rays sa isang focal point.
copy.bis: Ang convex lens mas baga sa tunga kay sa mga kilid, ug gipatigom niini ang parallel light rays sa usa ka focal point.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Convex lenses
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the trophic levels of an organism as levels of energy in a food pyramid
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes uses of convex lenses (optics). G7-L-9 concerns trophic levels and energy transfer in food pyramids, a biology topic with no connection to lenses.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Convex lenses
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to group animals according to the food they eat: plant eaters (herbivores), meat eaters (carnivores), and plant and meat-eaters (omnivores)
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about convex lens applications in magnifying glasses, cameras, and microscopes. G4-L-6 requires grouping animals by diet (herbivores, carnivores, omnivores), which is unrelated to lens optics.

copy.en: Convex lenses, which are converging lenses that bend light inward, are used in magnifying glasses, cameras, and microscopes to enlarge objects or focus images.
copy.tl: Ang mga convex lens, na mga converging lens na nagpapabaluktot ng liwanag papaloob, ay ginagamit sa magnifying glasses, cameras, at microscopes para palakihin ang mga bagay o i-focus ang mga imahe.
copy.bis: Ang mga convex lens, nga mga converging lens nga nagpabawog sa kahayag pasulod, gigamit sa magnifying glasses, cameras, ug microscopes aron padak-on ang mga butang o i-focus ang mga imahe.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A convex mirror, also called a diverging mirror, has a reflective surface that bulges outward and reflects light rays away from each other.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate various techniques in separating mixtures, such as decantation, winnowing, scooping, picking, evaporation, filtering, sieving, and using magnets
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the behavior of a convex mirror (diverging light), which is a physics/optics topic. G6-M-6 is about demonstrating techniques for separating mixtures (decantation, winnowing, filtering, etc.). There is no connection to mixtures or separation techniques.

copy.en: A convex mirror, also called a diverging mirror, has a reflective surface that bulges outward and reflects light rays away from each other.
copy.tl: Ang convex mirror, tinatawag ding diverging mirror, ay may reflective surface na nakaumbok palabas at nagre-reflect ng light rays palayo sa isa't isa.
copy.bis: Ang convex mirror, gitawag usab nga diverging mirror, adunay reflective surface nga nakaumbok pagawas ug nagre-reflect sa light rays palayo sa usag usa.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A convex mirror, which curves outward like the back of a spoon, always forms an upright, virtual image that is smaller than the object.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe living things, such as animals and plants, as biotic factors and light, water, temperature, and soil type, as abiotic factors in an ecosystem
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about convex mirror image formation (physics/optics). G6-L-7 is about biotic and abiotic factors in an ecosystem, a living-things topic. No overlap in content.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A convex mirror, which curves outward like the back of a spoon, always forms an upright, virtual image that is smaller than the object.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a drawing or diagram to classify some Philippine animals and plants, based on their habitat: some live on land (terrestrial), live in water (aquatic) or fly in the air (aerial)
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about convex mirror image formation (physics/optics). G4-L-3 requires a drawing/diagram classifying Philippine animals/plants by habitat. The card has no relation to living things or habitats.

copy.en: A convex mirror, which curves outward like the back of a spoon, always forms an upright, virtual image that is smaller than the object.
copy.tl: Ang convex mirror, na nakakurba palabas tulad ng likod ng kutsara, ay laging bumubuo ng nakatayong virtual image na mas maliit kaysa sa bagay.
copy.bis: Ang convex mirror, nga nagkurba paingon sa gawas sama sa likod sa kutsara, kanunay nga moporma og tul-id nga virtual image nga mas gamay kaysa sa butang.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The dry season is divided into a cool dry period from November to February and a hot dry period from March to April.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: express quantitatively the amount of solute present in a given volume of solvent
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the Philippine dry season periods (cool dry and hot dry). It contains no information about solute, solvent, or expressing the amount of solute quantitatively, which is the subject of G7-M-9.

copy.en: The dry season is divided into a cool dry period from November to February and a hot dry period from March to April.
copy.tl: Ang dry season ay nahahati sa cool dry period mula Nobyembre hanggang Pebrero at hot dry period mula Marso hanggang Abril.
copy.bis: Ang dry season gibahin ngadto sa cool dry period gikan sa Nobiyembre hangtod Pebrero ug hot dry period gikan sa Marso hangtod Abril.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Cooling speed changes crystal size! A hot salt solution cooled quickly makes small crystals.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore the school grounds or the local area to observe or collect different types of rocks, describing their similarities and differences in terms of features, such as texture, color, and grain crystal size
assignedReviews.reason: The competency is about exploring and collecting different types of rocks and describing their features (texture, color, grain crystal size). The card discusses crystal size in a salt solution due to cooling rate, which is not about rocks or rock features. It shares only the phrase 'crystal size' but does not support the rock-focused competency.

copy.en: Cooling speed changes crystal size! A hot salt solution cooled quickly makes small crystals. But if cooled slowly, it forms big crystals instead!
copy.tl: Binabago ng bilis ng paglamig ang sukat ng kristal! Ang mainit na solusyon ng asin na mabilis na pinalamig ay gumagawa ng maliliit na kristal. Pero kapag dahan-dahan, lumalaki ang mga ito!
copy.bis: Ang paspas sa pagbugnaw nagbag-o sa gidak-on sa kristal! Ang mainit nga solusyon sa asin nga paspas ang pagbugnaw naghimo og gagmay nga kristal. Apan kon hinay, nagporma og dagko nga kristal!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When an object is cooled, the average kinetic energy of its molecules decreases
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary resources to classify animals and plants of the Philippines as critically endangered, endangered, or vulnerable species
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains cooling and molecular kinetic energy, which is a physics/thermal energy concept. G9-L-6 requires classifying Philippine animals and plants as critically endangered, endangered, or vulnerable. There is no connection to biodiversity, endangered species, or Philippine organisms.

copy.en: When an object is cooled, the average kinetic energy of its molecules decreases, making them move slower and lowering the object's temperature.
copy.tl: Kapag pinalamig ang isang bagay, bumababa ang average na kinetic energy ng mga molecule nito, kaya mas mabagal silang gumagalaw at bumababa ang temperatura ng bagay.
copy.bis: Kung pabugnawan ang usa ka butang, mous-os ang average nga kinetic energy sa mga molecule, busa mas mohinay sila sa paglihok ug mous-os ang temperatura sa butang.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: After using the microscope, turn off the illuminator and let the bulb cool before storing it to extend its life.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about microscope bulb care, with no information about classifying living things into groups using a table.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: After using the microscope, turn off the illuminator and let the bulb cool before storing it to extend its life.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss in small groups important concepts in the theories of evolution, such as variation, heredity, isolation, selection, and adaptation
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses microscope maintenance, not evolution concepts such as variation, heredity, isolation, selection, or adaptation.

copy.en: After using the microscope, turn off the illuminator and let the bulb cool before storing it to extend its life.
copy.tl: Pagkatapos gamitin ang microscope, patayin ang illuminator at hayaang lumamig ang bulb bago itago para tumagal ito.
copy.bis: Human gamita ang microscope, palonga ang illuminator ug pabugnawan ang bulb sa dili pa tipigan aron molungtad kini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Cooling a liquid can change it back to a solid
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the process of photosynthesis and respiration, and identify its raw materials needed and products
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a phase change (cooling a liquid to a solid) and particle behavior. It has no content about photosynthesis or respiration, their raw materials, or products.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Cooling a liquid can change it back to a solid
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about cooling a liquid to a solid, not about observing outer parts of plants (leaves, roots, stems) or their roles in water/nutrient uptake.

copy.en: Cooling a liquid can change it back to a solid, because the particles slow down and lock into fixed positions again.
copy.tl: Ang pagpapalamig ng liquid ay maaaring magpabalik nito sa pagiging solid, dahil ang particles ay bumabagal at kumakapit muli sa kanilang puwesto.
copy.bis: Ang pagpabugnaw sa liquid makapabalik niini sa pagka-solid, tungod kay ang particles mohinay ug mobalik sa ilang nahimutangan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Copper is a metal with a shiny reddish-orange color
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the process of photosynthesis and respiration, and identify its raw materials needed and products
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a physical property of copper (a metal). It has no content about photosynthesis, respiration, or their raw materials and products.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Copper is a metal with a shiny reddish-orange color
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: using flow charts and labeled diagrams explain the role of plants and animals in the cycles of nature, such as the carbon, oxygen, and water cycles
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about copper's color, not about the role of plants and animals in carbon, oxygen, or water cycles, and it does not use flow charts or labeled diagrams.

copy.en: Copper is a metal with a shiny reddish-orange color, which makes it easy to recognize among other metals.
copy.tl: Ang tanso ay isang metal na may makintab na mapula-kahel na kulay, kaya madali itong makilala sa ibang mga metal.
copy.bis: Ang tumbaga usa ka metal nga adunay sinaw nga pula-kahel nga kolor, mao nga sayon kini nga mailhan taliwala sa laing mga metal.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Copper is preferred for water pipes because it is unreactive
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use diagrams and illustrations to describe the arrangement, spacing, and relative motion of the particles in each of the three states (phases) of matter
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses copper's chemical inertness and durability, not the arrangement, spacing, or motion of particles in the three states of matter, nor does it use diagrams or illustrations.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Copper is preferred for water pipes because it is unreactive
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume (solids: definite shape and volume; liquids: no definite shape, definite volume; gases: no definite shape or volume)
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a chemical property of copper, not the shape and volume properties of solids, liquids, and gases.

copy.en: Copper is preferred for water pipes because it is unreactive, meaning it does not easily combine with water or other substances, so it lasts a long time.
copy.tl: Ang copper ay ginagamit sa mga water pipe dahil ito ay unreactive, ibig sabihin hindi ito madaling makipag-ugnay sa tubig o ibang substance, kaya tumatagal ito nang husto.
copy.bis: Ang copper gigamit sa mga water pipe tungod kay kini unreactive, nagpasabot nga dili kini dali nga makig-uban sa tubig o uban nga substance, mao nga molungtad kini ug dugay.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Coral reef formation depends on temperature, light penetration, stable salinity, and water movement.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses coral reef formation, which is unrelated to the solar system, celestial objects, or their composition. The competency G5-E-11 requires describing the general structure of the solar system, which this card does not support.

copy.en: Coral reef formation depends on temperature, light penetration, stable salinity, and water movement.
copy.tl: Ang pagbuo ng coral reef ay nakadepende sa temperature, light penetration, stable salinity, at water movement.
copy.bis: Ang pagporma sa coral reef nagdepende sa temperature, light penetration, stable salinity, ug water movement.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Two parts bend light inside the eye: the clear cornea in front, and the lens inside.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion
assignedReviews.reason: The competency requires using models, flow charts, diagrams, or simulations to explain how body systems work together (e.g., digestion and excretion). The card only states which eye parts bend light; it does not address body systems working together, nor does it use any required representation. The content is unrelated to the competency.

copy.en:
What parts of the eye bend light?

Two parts bend light inside the eye: the clear cornea in front, and the lens inside.
copy.tl:
Anong bahagi ng mata ang nagliliko ng liwanag?

Dalawang bahagi ang nagliliko ng liwanag sa mata: ang malinaw na cornea sa harap at ang lente sa loob.
copy.bis:
Unsang bahin sa mata ang nagaliko sa kahayag?

Duha ka bahin ang nagaliko sa kahayag sa mata: ang tin-aw nga cornea sa atubangan ug ang lente sa sulod.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The cornea is the clear covering at the front of the eye that protects the inner parts from dust and dirt.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: apply science process skills and attitudes in conducting a guided survey about environmental issues and concerns including grouping and classifying, communicating, and open mindedness
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches eye anatomy (cornea function), which has no connection to conducting a guided survey about environmental issues or applying science process skills to environmental concerns.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The cornea is the clear covering at the front of the eye that protects the inner parts from dust and dirt.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify issues and concerns in the local community and how they could be addressed by science, such as the treatment of waste
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about the cornea protecting the eye, not about identifying local community issues and how science could address them, such as waste treatment.

copy.en: The cornea is the clear covering at the front of the eye that protects the inner parts from dust and dirt.
copy.tl: Ang cornea ay ang malinaw na takip sa harap ng mata na pumoprotekta sa mga panloob na bahagi nito mula sa alikabok at dumi.
copy.bis: Ang cornea mao ang tin-aw nga tabon sa atubangan sa mata nga moprotekta sa mga parte sa sulod niini batok sa abog ug hugaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The corpus luteum produces estrogen
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify how oceanic crust and continental crust is associated with the Earth's lithospheric plates
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes corpus luteum hormones (estrogen, progesterone) and uterine preparation for pregnancy, which is unrelated to oceanic/continental crust and lithospheric plates.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The corpus luteum produces estrogen
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to describe and explain what mechanisms that drive the movement of tectonic plates including the role of the asthenosphere
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about reproductive hormones, not tectonic plate movement mechanisms or the asthenosphere.

copy.en: The corpus luteum produces estrogen and large amounts of progesterone, a hormone that signals the uterus to thicken in preparation for pregnancy.
copy.tl: Ang corpus luteum ay gumagawa ng estrogen at maraming progesterone, isang hormone na nagsesenyas sa matris na kumapal bilang paghahanda sa pagbubuntis.
copy.bis: Ang corpus luteum naghimo og estrogen ug daghang progesterone, usa ka hormone nga nagsenyas sa matris nga mobag-on isip pagpangandam sa pagmabdos.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In the October 2019 Cotabato earthquakes, five of the twenty-two recorded fatalities were attributed to landslides.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes earthquake-related landslide fatalities in Cotabato. G5-E-11 requires describing the general structure of the solar system and major celestial objects. The card has no connection to the solar system, celestial objects, or their features/composition.
